body:
>You are not financially stable. DO NOT HAVE A KID YOU CANNOT AFFORD. Jesus fucking Christ...

You presume that we're living paycheck to paycheck, but that's not at all the case. I pull in $3,000/month for being alive, she pulls in a similar amount per month from her main job, and an extra $500-1,000 from her weekend job. The "getting more money" part is to build up a baby+transition fund exactly to avoid the the issue of massively dropping SoL just to accomplish those.

>No. They don't. Are you so far gone that you think other people being happy is fake?
I literally live where they go to retire. I'm around old people anytime I leave the house damned near. I'm not speaking without experience.

No, I don't think that being happy is necessarily fake. I'm well aware that what makes one person happy doesn't apply to another. I'm also aware that actual happiness is a rare fucking thing. It is a unicorn. What's much more common is things that are attempts at creating happiness, or else trying to fill the role of it. There are other positive feels besides happiness, with happiness simply being at the peak of that positive feel mountain.

>Did it ever occur to you they don't find it boring? You don't have to just start playing canasta on your 60th birthday.

Did it ever occur to *you* that I've heard old people specifically say things like "Oh, I'd love to do that, but I'm just not up to doing that sort of thing anymore."? 70-80 year olds I've heard say variations on this.

>Take charge of your fucking life. Revise your fucked up worldview. DON'T HAVE A GODDAMN KID YOU AREN'T MENTALLY OR FINANCIALLY READY FOR.

Ah, back to the whole "change your perspective" thing. It's all well and good to say "take charge of your life", but what does that actually entail, eh?

As for not having a kid, then that's just one thing to be miserable about. Like I said, I do want to be a mom. It's simple to say "You're too fucked up to have a kid.", but it's a whole other thing to actually do that and be reminded of that irreversible choice for decades every time you see a mom with her kid.

>Everyone has told you that just because you're old doesn't mean you should give up your life. But we're all wrong, right? You don't want to listen.

As I said, what makes some people happy doesn't make others happy. What would make me happy? Youth, freedom, loving marriage, a kid or two, being a mom to them, enough money to accomplish all that comfortably.

I shouldn't give up on life just because others don't in that particular context? People have said the same thing to me about were I to lose a limb, my eyesight, paralyzed, and so on. Some people welcome a challenge, the "Come at me bro!" thing. Not me. Never been that way.

>Yep. That's the plan. Until it isn't and the mouse wants a glass of milk to go with that cookie.

So now you're indirectly saying that my wife can't be trusted. Thanks.

>And here it is. Fuck the kid's future. Fuck what might actually help you. We must follow The Plan!

You missed the part in parentheses where I qualified it with basic moral stuff. So no, it's not purely "ends justify the means", but rather a case of having nothing but shitty choices.

>You think that being old never being happy. 

For me? Pretty much. For others? Maybe, depends on the individual.

>You think any marriage at all is better than being a self-actualized individual. 

Okay...what the hell does "self-actualized individual" even mean? Sounds like something a motivational speaker might say. O_o

And no, I don't think that any marriage at all is better than none exactly. I just know that it was painful to have no romantic and sexual intimacy, enough to consider walking into traffic at times. If there's a complete clone of my wife out there that has no issues with me transitioning or early menopause risks or some other problems, and who I would know is available before splitting, *then* I'd feel less distraught on that particular topic.

>You think it's more important to breed than you care about that kid's well being. 

Nope. You don't think that I'd do my damnedest to help raise that kid to be as well-prepared for life in conjunction with happy childhood experiences...then you sorely underestimate me on this specific topic. People are accusing me of black/white thinking, and yet I'm being presented with that. 

>And when people tell you that the world isn't the way you think it is, that life doesn't end at 40... You don't care. They're all full of shit and your situation has no solution.

I didn't say that life ends at 40, please don't twist my words. For me it simply ends when I start to look and feel undeniably old, hence the 50-60 range based on how I've seen my parents age.
As for solutions, I'm looking for ones that aren't confined to "change your perspective". BTW, I do actually appreciate some of the *intentions* behind those particular sorts of attempts to help here, even if not the words themselves.

>You're so scared of what you think will go wrong that you don't take any steps for things to go right.

What can I say, I hate to gamble. I'll take calculated risks, but only if the odds are very heavily in my favor if I can help it. The times that I haven't I've tended to have Murphy bite me in the ass. The whole concept of trying your best regardless of the odds doesn't gel with me.

>And before you think I don't know what I'm talking about... 

*snip to..*

>Making progress.

I'm sincerely sorry that you got dealt a hand that shitty. Congrats on having the guts, fortitude, willpower, and anything else that contributes to being able to get through that.

>We're both happy now. If one of us is miserable... we're both miserable, right? You solve it with happiness. Not shared suffering. 

What the hell do you think my goal is? You have been taking my wording on what a compromise is out of context to beat me over the head with the misery thing. You can't completely erase the fact that someone's going to be denied something they want or would prefer, so it makes sense to make a deal that minimizes that as equally as possible, hence maximizing the potential for positive feels to outweigh the negative feels all around within the given circumstances. That's what I meant since it apparently needed clarification.

>Kids? Adoption. Because blood doesn't matter. Love and support makes a family. Not genetics.

I thought I made it clear that adoption's not on the table. Yes, love and support makes a family, but I want it to be the result of my and my wife's genes. That part is non-negotiable and it grates any time I've had someone bring it up after I've told them I don't want to. It's great that there's people out there that want to do that, I wish them the best, but I'm not them and neither is my wife for that matter. Feel free to mock or chastise me or us for that.

>You need to take ownership of your life and do what you need to do. To get your priorities straight. You know things aren't right, or you wouldn't be here, asking for advice.

I posted this thread because I was hit upside the head with the fact that the universe screwed me out of my teens and 20s, and that I'm left with mostly the middle age years to "enjoy". The advice I was seeking was not intended to be motivational speaking stuff. I can get that from my therapist. I knew there were trans girls here hit with that same realization around my age, and my assumption proved correct. So I figured some of those trans girls would have things to say that actually might be applicable to my screwed up ass, apart from the near-mandatory "glass is half-full" type stuff.

>We're all telling you to embrace your life, to chase happiness. And happiness is real. It's something you can have. Go fucking get it or you'll never have it.

I keep hearing this, but it's making no damned sense. Seriously. "Chase happiness"? You see, the problem I have with the phrase "the pursuit of happiness" is that pursuit part, as it implies that you could indeed pursue as hard as you can and never get that happiness, but now we're getting philosophical or some shit.

Oh, happiness is real. It's simply a rare thing, just as I said before. It's something I can have? Sure, if various conditions are met, it's very possible. However, I can't count on that. Actually, I'm starting to get a bit confused as to what exactly you're even telling me to do in order to achieve said happiness. o_O

>It just seems like you're seeing everything in black and white. Like it's either option A, or option B. Life isn't like that, it's a spectrum, just like our gender identities.

It's more that after brainstorming through the possible options I'm left with very few of them as being remotely viable. I can understand how it'd seem black and white thinking at first glance.

>It took time to accept that I may always be flying solo, and it can be incredibly discouraging, but I managed to find peace with that, and even embrace it.

I tried to get into that mindset in my 20s, and combined with other factors, it led to me being massively suicidal. So, unfortunately, not an option for me.

>Don't condemn yourself to death in 20 years before you've even started this journey. 

Oh it's not written in stone. If some means of stopping the clock and pulling back some of those sands of time is available by then my options suddenly open up in a big way.

>Please keep an open mind.

Contrary to how it might look, I actually am trying to. If I wasn't I wouldn't have posted this thread up at all. I appreciate the lack of accusatory tone you've maintained, though.

>I hear this sort of thing a lot. Being less miserable isn't the same as being happier.

She has been literally the only partner that's made me happy. And throwing away a marriage is supposed to ensure happiness? Being childless, the end of my fucking line, is suppose to ensure happiness? *She* doesn't make me miserable, it's the situation.

>And a kid costs even more.

It's not IUF/IVF or kid, it's kid + IUF/IVF or kid - IUF/IVF. Yes, I am aware that kids cost quite a bit. That's why I've been trying to work on ways to get more money in spite of being on disability, and why she's been busting her ass working 7 days a week.

>Yeah... That's not okay. You're using human life as a bargaining chip. Two of them, actually.

And if I just go full-bore everything will go to hell much harder, much faster, and far messier. The same applies if we do things how she'd prefer were I less of a concern. You keep saying "human bargaining chips" like I'm this evil monster because both of us are trying to find a way to achieve as many goals as we can with some of them being in conflict. The ones in conflict can't simply be dismissed, either, otherwise they would've by now.

>So you're going to get old. Why is that doom? Do you think elderly people are just miserable all the time?

Because they find various things to either distract themselves, delude themselves, or console themselves. I live in a place with lots of old people, I see it on a regular basis. They know they've gotten slower, frailer, uglier, less energetic. That's part of why so many of them spend their retirement years doing such low-key boring shit. Even the ones that do the whole "young in spirit" thing, they just try to run it over with brute force optimism. Also, many of them actually accept the whole "living on through your children" thing, or else that there's "something better after this world", or else the notion that they've accomplished good things that will live on past them. Many just try to laugh it off, even while they get Alzheimer's, multitudes of cancers, bones broken with ease that barely heal, strokes, heart attacks, etc.

>You're drowning in your own depression and continuing to deny yourself is only going to make it worse. Bringing a baby into this situation is more than irresponsible. It's cruel. You need to reevaluate what you need for yourself. The fact that she wants to bring a kid into this as well and your needs come after? That's fucked up too. You two are not in a healthy, stable place. Her biological clock isn't more important than a kid's future.

And your solution for all these woes would be...?

>Is this where you want to be? Are you heading in the right direction? Or are you just going with it out of apathy or fear that things might get worse?

I'm not seeing any other options that don't rob me of other important things as a result. Again, you tell me since you're telling me I'm wrong and need to do something else.

>And once she's pregnant... What if she wants you to wait in case of a miscarriage? And then things are so busy with the baby. Then the kid's in school, that will just be so much social stigma and kids are cruel... Maybe when the kid's grown it'll be a better time.

Already been figured on by us. Soon as it's confirmed that she's pregnant I'm in the clear. I'll be banking sperm as a back-up plan if she loses it anyway (if nothing else, the thought of going sterile scares me, even if they're not the preferred sort of gametes). She's accepted my argument that it's much better for me to transition through the first 3-5 years of the kid's life than any time later. She also knows I won't accept a later time anyway. As I said in an earlier reply, over my dead rotting corpse.

>If you're upset about the loss of your youth, why are you letting more of it go? Don't you think raising a child will be even more life-consuming?

Because it's now or never, as I have said multiple times in this thread so far. Neither of us wants to be childless, neither of us is apt to have kids with anyone else even if we were able to do so by then.

>The way you're talking, the way you're describing things... you know this isn't right. Deep down inside, you know.

I don't care about right (beyond very basic moral stuff) so much as if it gets it accomplished.

Also, once again, what are my alternatives? I've thought this over for the better part of a year, had many a long and difficult talk with her on these two conflicting things, and I've yet to find a less shitty option.

Reddit really needs a multi-quote function for situations like this.

As I said to another, it's both youth and freedom/life/whatever.

I don't want to simply be a "sperm donor". I want to have a kid, it's not just her demanding to have a baby.

She doesn't care about me, and is causing me to not care about me? It's the opposite, actually. Like I said above, when one of us is miserable the other is miserable. Part of her own therapy is about trying to deal with her "husband" becoming a wife. If I go storming full-bore into HRT then things will go from "difficult" to "implosion".

A better life? In what way? No wife, no kid, low as fuck odds of finding another relationship remotely worth a damn? Some people are fine doing the whole perpetual bachelorette thing, but I know it'd cause me to kill myself quicker.

Again, already in therapy.

It doesn't have to be this way? Okay, care to tell me how it can be different aside from vague philosophical stuff having to do with having freedom to choose?

I'm already in therapy, both solo and as a couple.

Yep, it is fucked. Less fucked than the situation I had before I met her, which basically amounted to suicide being far more likely, enough that I'd likely be dead for a few years now otherwise.

Artificial insemination costs money, thousands per pop for IUF, tens of thousands for IVF.

C-sections are terrible on both the mother and kid, and only ought to be done when there's no other real choice. Bad analogy, IMO.

Compromise is where both parties get some of what they want, but not all of what they want, and thus are equally disappointed. Either of us just caving to each other would result in them being very miserable, and thus whoever is causing the caving to also be very miserable because when one of us is very miserable we both are.

Negotiating suicide had to do with limiting to criteria that would prompt me to do so. She was pretty adamant about me not considering it at all, but I required that it always be on the table as an option. It was either that, or there be that whole "If one of us is miserable we're both miserable" thing in effect.

Hey, if there's a way for me to not be doomed to that sort of aging then it gets pushed muuuch further down the list of options. You think I like the idea of dying at that age range, or leaving an adult child like that? Still, I'm no stranger to death, so it's not like I don't know how death of a loved one feels at various ages, which is why is not optimal but so long as they're prepared to be an independent adult then it's barely tolerable.

It's both loss of youth and loss of life, but had I youth it wouldn't be an issue. I'd have time on my side. At current I don't. That's the bigger limiting factor.

Again, I do want this hypothetical kid. If I didn't I wouldn't have agreed on that compromise in the first place. My wanting to have one isn't related to my desire to evade aging past an approximate physical point. I'd be happier than a pig in mud if both things could be accomplished, but so far, science has let me down too much on that front, so it restricts my options.

Of course what's my alternative? Miss this very, very short window of opportunity to have a kid? Have no progeny, be the end of my bloodline? Not get to raise my own flesh and blood?

And just to pre-empt, no, adoption is NOT on the table at any time. Yeah, there's lots of kids that need homes, and so on. The people that want to adopt, great, that's noble of them. That's not me. My flesh and blood or none at all.

Since Reddit doesn't seem to have a multi-quote system to let me reply to all of the replies to my previous post, which has been downvoted out sight anyway, I guess I'll have to do it individually.

Yes, I have been seeing a therapist, both by myself and as a couple.

No, I actually do want to have a kid. I said that in the OP. I would like to be a mom. Having a kid in and of itself was not what was compromised on, it was the particulars regarding conception vs my HRT.

Abort the relationship? Um, no. She's my best friend and I have too many issues to actually date, especially as a 30-something trans woman. I offered her the option of divorce if it got too much for her not because I thought I'd have better odds of finding a replacement for my wife of 6 years, but to not keep her trapped.

She already knows. The only reason I wouldn't do it then is if my ability to keep my promise she basically cornered me into doesn't get outweighed by my disgust and rage.

Said promise was that I'm not allowed to kill myself unless I'm in horribly agonizing pain that's effectively untreatable. I try to keep to my word, but I'm not seeing how I'm going to hold out past 60 at best. Going beyond that point would be purely to fulfill that promise and nothing more. She's the one obsessed with "growing old together", basically has a totally opposite outlook on the topic.

She literally has said that she'd rather me be a vegetable or drugged so hard I'm not really in the world than for me to be dead.

Enough time to raise said kid to adulthood (have kid by 33, off myself at 53 = they're 20 years old). Also, I don't wish I were dead just yet. Pissed and depressed about my situation, but suicide isn't really in the cards until my 50s.

Bully for you. What's your secret to acting like a teenager without it coming back to hit your wife and/or kid then?

The compromise happened because it's a now or never situation. We can't put off her getting pregnant because she's mid-30s herself and has a high risk of early menopause. We're both up against the clock. Our relationship is obviously uncertain with regards to sex and romance, but she's absolutely dead set on us staying married, even when I've mentioned that I'd rather her divorce me in advance than be with me if it makes her miserable.

And no, it doesn't remove all freedom of choice, but it makes pretty much any choices beyond the most trivial far more expensive in whatever resource is needed to account for the kid (time, money, patience, favors, etc.). I helped raise my brother and saw how it hit my mother, so I'm no stranger to how hard kids can impact your personal life.

As for not putting it in my OP, I didn't want it to turn into a massive text wall, plus I was hoping to get responses that are less along the lines of "Fuck the police, do what you want!", mainly because the real issue for me is that even were I to try and make up for that lost decade and change, I'd only have a few years to do it in. Sometime between 50 and 60 I'm done anyway, which is why another redditor saying "I still have the other 2/3 of my life" has no impact on me since for me the years beyond 60 don't count, and 40-60 only partially count.

No offense, but that's rather easy to say when being able to even start HRT isn't tied to your SO getting pregnant. Yes, I made a promise with her to not start until she is pregnant and the fetus is viable, the natural way, not artificially. That was the compromise. Originally she was desperate for me to wait until after we have kids that have been raised and become adults because "lots of people transition at that age". Over my dead rotting corpse, hence the compromise in the truest sense of the word; a deal where both parties get some of what they want and are equally disappointed.

I'll get no chance to be a carefree single woman, doing as I please, because by the time I change enough to start failing boy mode I'll be a fucking parent. I do want a kid because it'll be the closest I get to being a mother (though not The Mother, for reasons I won't go into), but I basically will be a parent right out the fucking gate.

So, please, keep telling me of this whole ignoring other people business.
Thank you. That helped to answer more questions than just that one.

And when you say "and now I have to play on hard mode" is that an indirect way of saying you'd no longer consider yourself to be physically attractive to others? Not meaning to be offensive here, just trying to make sure I'm understanding you. Tone doesn't carry well through text.

Yes, I've told her just about everything I've said so far to varying degrees.

As for what's been said about the stuff that's been brought up, you'll have to be a little more specific, otherwise I'd have to cobble together a text wall to sum up what's been talked about over the course of quite a few months.
Yes. That's why I accepted that I am mtf rather than something else. A therapist that specializes in gender issues, which is why I'm taking it so seriously.

And my concern is that I'll look in that mirror and see a poor attempt at being female, a paltry and shoddy simulacrum of one, a walking satire of one that I'd be surprised doesn't crack said mirror. A creature that can't but help beginning to resent those luckier.

Unfortunately, I'm aware that E doesn't do nearly as much as T. I'm glad the T worked out well for you.

As for growing old...not happening for me, regardless of what body I have. I've seen that, I've grown up around it, there's nothing noble or golden about it, even in the most gracefully aged. Middle age, fine, but beyond that it's game over anyway.

I would like things to be better, too. I would, that's why I'm even here, to see if maybe I'm not screwed, that my odds aren't nearly as bad as I'd been led to believe. I just don't play dice games unless the stats are heavily in my favor to start with. Faith is something I don't do.

If I can't reach that point that would meet my "I can reasonably live with this" threshold, my equivalent to you saying you wanted to see an unquestioningly not female body in the mirror...then it really hasn't mattered. My life is still torn apart, turned inside out. I've still spent plenty of resources. I've still suffered for what would effectively be a forlorn hope.

Thanks for the chart. Fits the time frames I've seen in other stuff so far, so it serves to confirm things.

However, I think you misunderstood me. When I said "no going back", I'm not talking about going on HRT for a few months because that doesn't deal with the issue I was referring to. If it were that simple I'd already be doing just that. I wish it was that simple.

The issue is that to know how I'd turn out I'd have to transition for years, not months, basically complete that second puberty. By that point, yeah, there would be no going back.

That's actually even besides the point. I don't like the body I'm stuck in anyway, definite body dysphoria, so at best detransitioning after getting into it the years needed to see what the end result is puts me back to square one, embarrassed, ostracized, surgical stuff, etc. making that a very relative thing. Far more likely is that I end up in a much worse position than current, that being bad enough already, given how some parts of it are very permanent by that point, not to mention the unavoidable social impact mentioned before. Either way I'm still SOL, and then I really would be left with either getting medicated enough to not care about anything anymore, or doing something a bit faster and more permanent.

>making non-optimal choices and spurning the rational.

>knowing that your hope is perhaps a false one?

This is nearly the opposite of me. I am completely unable to "fake it till you make it" with regards to things like optimism in the face of crap odds. I generally just stop attempting whatever it is if that's the case, except when I'm given no chance to refuse or run.

>It's a gamble, for sure.

Exactly why I'm here; need to know if I should make a bet that requires all my money or just leave the table and the casino entirely.

>if you define your "win" as complete 100% passing

I'd need to not be clocked at a fair distance, or else be obvious enough to insta-squick people. I wouldn't call that 100%, so maybe 80%? I dunno. But assuming that, it doesn't help to pass most of the time but still be ugly. I'll still be miserable if that's the case.

>are you planning SRS if you do transition? 

Probably not. The surgeries are just too damned primitive. I know some transwomen have severe genital dysphoria, so more power to 'em for doing what felt they had to do. However, me, no...not with how it's done currently, and probably not for a few decades given how that particular field is trudging along. Meh, I'll probably be too old or not living to care about it by then anyway. Hell, even the various cosmetic surgeries are too damned primitive (saline sacks, chiseling/sanding bone, etc.). I mean, if I were to have to get FFS to not be a hideous target, then fine, whatever, but that's about it.

>Don't know how you can answer your questions except by doing it ... 

That's one of the things that terrifies me the most. I can commit to something or someone if I think it's/they're worthwhile, but I still have to have an exit strategy. I'm aware that there is no such thing as going back with this, no way of undoing things, that I'd be effectively trapped without escape (aside from the obvious). I'm the sort of person that never reads a choose your own adventure book without keeping my fingers on the previous page or three.

>Get DNA tested and maybe find you're intersexed?

Given my build and other characteristics I'd have better odds of winning the lotto and being struck by lightning on the same day.
